restrictions: Two distinct inputs (x, 0) and (y, 0), x != y canonical Pallas field elements, rho = 0, for the complete Orchard hash with all 56 partial rounds (poseidon-orchard-r56-prefix-v1): found as a collision F(x) = F(y) of the walk F(x) = digest(x, 0), whose output is again a canonical input. Plain birthday search with one trail and distinguished points; no property of the rounds is used.

Machine, the cost model's own: Pallas field RAM with 256-bit words, one call of the reference permutation = 1 unit (C = 1392), every other word operation 1/1392. The trail step is 1 unit + 7 other operations (proof.md Section 5); recovery evaluations 1 unit + 8; all table and bookkeeping work is bounded by 10^8 operations. time_log2 is the full budget (every halt charged at its limit): S = n + d trail steps, 3 gmax recovery evaluations, with n the least multiple of 2^100 that reaches success 0.39 (proof.md Section 4, `python3 rho.py --plan` on proof.md Appendix B). One attempt, no restart, no amplification, no advice, no preprocessing.

Memory: a table of 2^14 + 2 entries of 48 bytes (786,528) plus at most 21,600 bytes of code, 6,464 bytes of constants and 512 bytes of registers: 815,104 bytes, below 2^20; claimed as 2^20, so the memory term of the score is zero.

Success probability at least 0.39: Lemma 2 of proof.md Section 4 proves it for a uniformly random function F (bound 0.3900000006) from the lazy-sampling hazard (i + 1) / N of each fresh step, with explicit terms for detection, table and gaps; H1 (declared, score-critical) says the real attempt succeeds at least as often.

The program is printed in full in proof.md Appendix B (standard library only; no outside code or library); no experiments are declared. No collision of the full target is produced here and none is claimed to be producible here; the claim is the cost of the search.

heuristics.statement: Model premise. Let F be a uniformly random function from the Pallas field (N = p, about 2^254) to itself and the distinguished-point set (density theta = 27554 / 2^128) independent of F. For the fixed target, the probability that the single attempt of the search succeeds on the walk x -> digest(x, 0) is at least the probability P_F, over a uniform 254-bit start and F, that the same search succeeds when every evaluation is replaced by F (lazy sampling): (a) the iterates have the first-collision law of a random mapping (each fresh step hits one of the i + 1 earlier values with probability (i + 1) / N); (b) whether an iterate is a distinguished point is independent of the collision events and of the other iterates, with probability theta. Proof.md Section 4 proves P_F >= 0.39 for F.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target poseidon-orchard-r56-prefix-v1 restricted to inputs (x, 0), one trail of about 1.7e38 evaluations of F from a uniform 254-bit start. Not claimed for other messages, other round counts, or other evaluation counts.
heuristics.extrapolation: Declared and not proved; no proof is known. The functional graph of F on 2^254 points and trails of 2^127 steps cannot be observed. No experiment is declared; no number of the claim is estimated from a run. Extrapolation to width 254 is by the premise only. If the hazard is (1 - e) / N instead of 1 / N the budget needs 0.0072 bit for e = 0.01, 0.0370 bit for e = 0.05, 0.076 bit for e = 0.10.
heuristics.limitations: A model premise about one fixed function, not a theorem: the run is a deterministic function of the start. It cannot be tested at width 254. The bound has no margin above 0.39 (n is the least multiple of 2^100 that reaches it), so any hazard deficit is repaired by extra time, priced above.

heuristics.statement: The call of the reference permutation is one unit and pays for all of its arithmetic, constants and loads (the cost model's definition of the target-compression unit); the loop variables are registers; the other operations are charged at 1/1392 as listed in proof.md Section 5 (7 per trail step, 8 per recovery evaluation, 10^8 for everything else).
heuristics.scope: The loop of one trail step, the recovery and the bounded bookkeeping of proof.md Section 5.
heuristics.extrapolation: None beyond the stated charges. If a loop step cost 20 other operations instead of 7 the time would rise by 0.0135 bit.
heuristics.limitations: The benchmark profile fixes no register count or instruction encoding; the code size of 36 bytes per instruction with 256-bit immediates is this entry's own convention, and memory has a one-MiB floor in the score.
